entities.name: Abul Hasan ash-Shadhili
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abu al-Hasan al-Shadhili was a Moroccan Islamic scholar and Sufi who founded the Shadhili Sufi order.

Born in the mid-12th century in Marrakech, Morocco, al-Shadhili was a prolific writer and mystic who drew upon the teachings of the Islamic mystics and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad.

Al-Shadhili's teachings emphasized the importance of spiritual purification, self-discipline, and the attainment of spiritual enlightenment through the practice of Sufi rituals and devotional practices.

He was a key figure in the spread of Sufism throughout North Africa and the Middle East, and his teachings had a significant impact on the development of Islamic mysticism.

Al-Shadhili's legacy continued to inspire Sufi mystics and scholars for centuries, and he remains one of the most important figures in the history of Islamic mysticism.

The Shadhili Sufi order, which was founded by al-Shadhili, continues to exist today, with adherents in many countries around the world.
